project keeps chosen columns, extend adds calculated ones, summarize aggregates (such as count by account and by one hour bins), and top, order by, take and distinct trim results. For text, has matches whole terms and is fast, while contains matches any substring and is slower. Defender tables use **Timestamp** and Sentinel tables use **TimeGenerated**.
Combining data

join links tables on a shared column. The default kind removes duplicates on the left side, inner keeps all matches, leftouter keeps unmatched left rows, and **leftanti** returns rows with no match, ideal for never seen before logic. union stacks rows from several tables, and let defines a variable or sub query.
Handy functions

summarize with **arg_max** returns the latest full row per device or user. make_set builds a list of distinct values and dcount counts them. FileProfile adds prevalence and signer details to file hashes. Priya joins email attachment hashes to file events to find attachments that landed on disk.

check.q: Priya wants admin accounts that signed in this week but never in the previous 90 days. Which join kind expresses no match on the other side?
check.why: leftanti returns left rows that have no match on the right, which is exactly new compared with history. inner returns matches, leftouter keeps everything on the left, and union is not a join at all.

lessons.key: KQL pipes a table through where, project, extend and summarize, and joins such as leftanti find activity never seen before.

lessons.title: Advanced hunting queries in Defender XDR
steps: Two modes

Advanced hunting is under Investigation and response, Hunting. **Guided mode** builds queries by choosing conditions, with no KQL needed. **Advanced mode** is a full KQL editor with a schema browser and sample queries. Queries can be saved to My queries or Shared queries for the team.
Quotas

Each query can reach 30 days of Defender XDR data and return up to 100,000 rows, within a size limit and a 10 minute timeout. Heavy use is metered per tenant, so filtering early on time and indexed terms keeps hunts fast and inside limits.
Sentinel data in the same place

When Sentinel is onboarded, its workspace tables appear in the same schema with the workspace's analytics retention. That is how Priya hunts Defender data older than 30 days when it is kept in Sentinel. Data held only in the data lake tier is not queryable here.
From hunt to detection

A query that finds something worth catching every time becomes a **custom detection** with Create detection rule, as covered earlier: it must return Timestamp and ReportId (and DeviceId for device tables), and can take automatic actions.

check.q: Priya needs to hunt Defender endpoint data from 60 days ago. Larkhill keeps those tables in Sentinel's analytics tier for 180 days. Where can she query it?
options: Only in the device's own timeline
Nowhere, Defender data is gone after 30 days
check.why: Onboarded Sentinel tables appear in advanced hunting with their own retention, so 60 day old data kept in the analytics tier is queryable there. Native Defender data stops at 30 days, which is the tempting wrong answer.

lessons.key: Advanced hunting offers guided and KQL modes with 30 days of native data, and onboarded Sentinel tables extend that with their own retention.

lessons.title: Interpreting threat analytics
steps: What threat analytics is

**Threat analytics** in the Defender portal publishes reports by Microsoft security researchers on active threats. Its dashboard highlights the latest threats, **high impact threats** (most alerts in your tenant) and **highest exposure threats** (based on how many of your devices could be exploited).
Report types
Reports cover an **activity** or campaign, an **actor** with its motives and techniques, a **tool**, a **technique**, a **vulnerability**, and curated open source intelligence.
Report tabs

The **analyst report** has a summary, technical detail, MITRE techniques, vetted **hunting queries** and recommendations. **Related incidents** and **impacted assets** show your own exposure. **Recommended actions** and **indicators** help you respond.
Using it at Larkhill

When a report on a banking trojan campaign appears, Priya opens its related incidents to check whether Larkhill is affected, runs its hunting queries in advanced hunting, and turns the best one into a custom detection. Access needs a Defender product licence beyond Defender for Endpoint Plan 1 alone.

check.q: A threat analytics report describes a ransomware group. Where does Priya see whether any Larkhill devices already have alerts linked to it?
options: The indicators tab of the report
check.why: Related incidents and impacted assets show the report's link to your own environment. The technical overview and MITRE section describe the threat in general, and indicators list signs to look for rather than existing alerts.

lessons.key: Threat analytics reports explain threats, provide vetted hunting queries, and show your related incidents, impacted assets and recommended actions.

lessons.title: Hunting graphs, blast radius and Sentinel graph
steps: Why graphs
Tables struggle to show chains such as a user who can sign in as a service principal that has rights on a key vault. The **hunting graph** in advanced hunting draws those chains as nodes and edges.
Hunting graph scenarios

Predefined scenarios include attack paths to a critical asset, paths between two entities, access to key vaults, users with access to sensitive data and paths to domain admins. Filters show only shortest paths or limit source and target nodes, such as internet exposed or holding sensitive data. It needs the Sentinel data lake onboarded and read access to Security Exposure Management.
Blast radius

**Blast radius** combines exposure data with incident data. From an incident graph, selecting a node and View blast radius shows the top possible attack paths from it to critical assets. Paths are possibilities, not confirmed activity, and results are only as good as the asset classification in Exposure Management.
Microsoft Sentinel graph

**Microsoft Sentinel graph** is the graph layer of the Sentinel platform, switched on with the data lake. KQL can turn exposure graph tables into a graph and match patterns such as a node linked through one to three hops. Custom graphs can be built from data lake data. Priya uses the paths to domain admins scenario to find which helpdesk accounts sit on a short path to Larkhill's domain.

check.q: Priya wants to see every chain by which an ordinary account could reach Larkhill's domain admins. Which tool fits best?
options: A blast radius view from any incident
A Sentinel workbook of group changes
An Audit (Standard) search of role changes
check.why: Hunting graph scenarios such as paths to domain admins show every relationship chain to a target. Blast radius starts from an incident node rather than all accounts, and workbooks and audit searches list events rather than paths.

lessons.key: Hunting graphs and blast radius show relationship chains and possible attack paths, built on the Sentinel data lake and graph.

lessons.title: Sentinel hunting queries and bookmarks
steps: The hunting page

Sentinel's **hunting** page lists queries installed from Content hub solutions plus custom ones, each with its data source, MITRE tactics and a **results delta** comparing the last 24 hours with the 24 before. N/A means the required data is not connected. Analysts can run all, selected or favourite queries.
Creating queries

A new hunting query needs a name, KQL, entity mappings and MITRE tactics and techniques. Content hub queries are cloned before editing. A query worth automating can become an analytics rule with one click. Microsoft suggests running relevant hunts at least weekly.
Bookmarks

Selecting interesting rows and choosing add **bookmark** saves the rows, the query and the time range, with entity mappings, tags and notes. Bookmarks are stored in the HuntingBookmark table and can create or join incidents.
Hunts

The **hunts** feature tracks a hypothesis driven hunt from start to finish, with its own queries, bookmarks and entities, a hypothesis state and outcomes such as new incidents or rules. Livestream is no longer available, so ongoing monitoring means converting the query to an analytics rule or a scheduled KQL job.

check.q: During a hunt, Priya finds three suspicious sign ins she wants to keep with their query and time range for later investigation. What should she create?
check.why: Bookmarks preserve the rows, query and time range with notes and can be turned into incidents. Tuning rules suppress alerts, summary rules aggregate data, and commitment tiers are about pricing.

lessons.key: Sentinel hunting queries show results deltas and MITRE mapping, bookmarks preserve findings, and hunts track hypotheses end to end.

lessons.title: KQL jobs in the Sentinel data lake
steps: Querying the lake

The **Sentinel data lake** holds large volumes of logs cheaply for up to 12 years. Interactive KQL queries run in data lake exploration. **KQL jobs** run queries as background work and save the results to a table.
Creating a job

A job has a name, a destination workspace and table (new or existing), the query and source workspaces, and a schedule: **one time** or **scheduled** by minute, hour, day, week or month. Scheduled jobs start at least 30 minutes after creation.
Destinations

Results can go to the **analytics tier**, where new tables get a _KQL_CL suffix and can feed rules and workbooks, or to the data lake tier with a _KQL suffix. Appending to an existing table needs a matching schema or the job fails.
Limits

Five jobs can run at once per tenant (extra runs are rejected, not queued), each has a one hour timeout, and up to 100 can be enabled. Some functions, such as externaldata and user defined functions, are not supported. New lake data can take up to 15 minutes to be queryable, so scheduled jobs end their window slightly in the past. Priya runs a daily job that copies firewall connections to known bad countries into an analytics table.

check.q: Larkhill's raw firewall logs live only in the data lake. Priya wants a small daily extract available to analytics rules. What should she create?
options: A workbook pointed at the data lake table
A scheduled KQL job into an analytics table
An NRT rule querying the data lake table
A hunting bookmark refreshed every day
check.why: A scheduled KQL job can query the lake and write results to an analytics table, where rules can use them. Workbooks and analytics rules cannot query lake only tables, and bookmarks only save hunting results.

lessons.key: KQL jobs query the data lake on a one time or scheduled basis and write results to analytics or lake tables, within concurrency and timeout limits.

lessons.title: Summary rules
steps: Making big data small

Raw logs such as firewall or proxy events are often kept on cheap plans because of their volume. **Summary rules** aggregate that data in the background and store the much smaller result in a custom table on the **analytics** plan, where hunting queries, workbooks and rules run quickly.
Creating one

Under Sentinel configuration, summary rules, Priya gives a name, a destination table ending in _CL, the KQL, and a schedule: a bin size from 20 minutes to a day, with an optional delay. Content hub includes summary rule templates. It needs Microsoft Sentinel Contributor.
Query rules
The query should not filter on time itself, because the bin defines the time range. Some functions and cross workspace calls are not allowed, and each workspace can have up to 100 active rules.
Using the results

Each result row carries the rule name, bin size and bin start time, and the table is queried like any other. Priya summarises hourly bytes per destination from the proxy logs, then hunts the small summary table for unusual data transfers instead of scanning billions of raw rows.

check.q: Why does Priya avoid adding a time filter to her summary rule's query?
options: Time filters hide results from other analysts
Summary rules cannot read the TimeGenerated column
The bin size sets each run's window
Time filters are only supported in KQL jobs
check.why: The summary rule's bin sets the window each run covers, so an extra time filter would conflict with it. The other statements do not describe how summary rules work.

lessons.key: Summary rules aggregate high volume logs on a schedule into small analytics tables, with the bin size defining each run's time range.

lessons.title: Notebooks and the Sentinel MCP server
steps: When code helps

Some hunts need code: machine learning, long baselines or custom graphs. **Jupyter notebooks** on the Sentinel data lake run in VS Code with the Microsoft Sentinel extension. Analysts pick a small, medium or large compute pool, and read lake tables into data frames with the Sentinel provider.
Writing and scheduling

Results can be saved as new tables, with an _SPRK suffix in the lake or _SPRK_CL in the analytics tier. Notebooks can run as scheduled jobs with an eight hour timeout. They support Python only, with a fixed set of libraries.
The Sentinel MCP server

**Model Context Protocol (MCP)** is an open standard that lets an AI assistant call tools exposed by a server. Microsoft hosts a **Sentinel MCP server** with collections such as data exploration and triage. Data exploration tools list workspaces, search for relevant tables, run KQL on the lake, and analyse a user or URL.
Connecting

In VS Code, an analyst adds an MCP server with HTTP transport, pastes the collection address, signs in with at least Security Reader, and uses chat in agent mode. Priya asks the assistant to find tables about VPN sign ins and draft a query, then checks the query herself before running it.

check.q: Priya wants an AI assistant in VS Code to search Larkhill's Sentinel lake tables and run KQL for her. What does she connect?
options: A Logic App playbook with an HTTP trigger
The Defender XDR advanced hunting API
check.why: The Sentinel MCP server exposes tools such as table search and lake queries to AI assistants over the Model Context Protocol. A playbook or API could be scripted, but neither gives an assistant ready made tools, and a notebook kernel runs code rather than serving tools.

lessons.key: Notebooks run Python hunts on the data lake from VS Code, and the Sentinel MCP server lets AI assistants search tables and run KQL.
